chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Yunus, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who gave birth and then saw blood more than she used to see.

He said: Let her refrain for the days of her menstrual period during which she used to sit, then let her seek precaution up to ten days. If she sees flowing blood, then let her perform ghusl (ritual bath) at the time of every salat (prayer); and if she sees yellowish discharge, then let her perform wudu (ablution) and then pray.

His statement عليه السلام, 'she seeks precaution by ten days,' means up to ten days, because particles with descriptive functions may stand in place of one another, as we have already explained in discussion of this.

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرُ: she takes precaution by extending consideration of bleeding to the legal limit
key_terms.قُرْئِهَا: her menstrual period or habitual cycle

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about a woman whose postnatal bleeding continues beyond her usual period?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding postnatal bleeding that extends beyond a woman's customary pattern. It instructs her to observe the days of her usual cycle, then consider the limit up to ten days, while distinguishing between flowing blood and yellowish discharge for the purposes of ghusl (ritual bath), wudu (ablution), and salat (prayer). The final sentence clarifies the wording of the ruling linguistically.
